sections.note: The goal of this one-credit course is to promote community within the cohort of first- and second-year undergraduate mathematics majors. The course includes lectures and panel discussions on the Illinois mathematics major and the various concentrations, panel discussions on ancillary topics (REU programs, internships, study abroad, departmental student organizations and clubs, undergraduate research opportunities, careers in mathematics, life in graduate school), and presentations from faculty on mathematical topics distinct from the calculus curriculum. An important aim of the course is to provide a venue for math majors to meet each other and to interact – outside of their usual classes – with faculty and graduate students. Such interactions are particularly important for current undergraduates, who experienced significant disruption in their K-12 education due to the COVID pandemic and whose social life within the department continues to be constrained by the ongoing building renovations.
